items.quote: Recovery strategy selection should align with specific athletic goals.
limitations: Pools earlier studies: it is only as strong as the studies it includes.
items.why: Recovery is when the adaptations from training actually happen.

items.title: Effects of Continuous and Cluster-Set Configurations Performed to Failure on Performance and Physiological Responses in the Bench Press and Half Squat
items.source: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
items.source_title: Effects of Continuous and Cluster-Set Configurations Performed to Failure on Performance and Physiological Responses in the Bench Press and Half Squat
items.authors: Tsoukos A, Ververis A, Bogdanis GC.
items.summary: Randomised controlled trial, published in Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports in July 2026. The study's title: "Effects of Continuous and Cluster-Set Configurations Performed to Failure on Performance and Physiological Responses in the Bench Press and Half Squat." Read the source for its methods and full results.
items.quote: The elevated cardiovascular and metabolic stress observed under CS20 reflects the substantially greater total work performed rather than an inherent effect of the cluster configuration.
limitations: A single study: one result is a data point, not a final answer.
items.why: Technique details decide how much of each rep your target muscles actually do.

items.title: Effects of standalone plyometric training on vertical jump and linear sprint performance in handball athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.source_title: Effects of standalone plyometric training on vertical jump and linear sprint performance in handball athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.authors: Zhang C, Wang Q.
items.summary: Systematic review, published in Frontiers in physiology in June 2026. The study's title: "Effects of standalone plyometric training on vertical jump and linear sprint performance in handball athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis." items.quote: Future research should establish standardized handball-specific plyometric protocols to refine evidence-based conditioning guidelines.
limitations: Pools earlier studies: it is only as strong as the studies it includes.
items.why: New training research is how coaching advice gets refined over time.

items.title: How much activity do adults need?
items.source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
items.source_title: Adult Activity: An Overview
items.summary: CDC's guidance for adults is about 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity each week, plus muscle-strengthening activity on at least 2 days a week.
items.why: Your DrukFit lifting days cover the strength part. Walks, cardio finishers and active rest days help with the rest.

items.title: How much sleep is enough?
items.source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), NIH
items.source_title: How Much Sleep Is Enough?
items.summary: NHLBI says experts recommend that adults sleep between 7 and 9 hours a night, and notes that adults who regularly sleep less than 7 hours may have more health problems.
items.why: Sleep is when your body recovers from training. Logging it in DrukFit shows how it relates to how your sessions feel.

items.title: Why regular physical activity matters
items.source_title: Physical activity (fact sheet)
items.summary: WHO's fact sheet sets out the health benefits of regular physical activity and the risks of inactivity, and notes that muscle strengthening benefits everyone.
items.why: A useful reminder of why showing up for your plan matters beyond how you look.

items.title: Does extra protein add to the gains from lifting?
items.source_title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults
items.authors: Morton RW, et al.
items.summary: This meta-analysis pooled randomised trials in healthy adults doing resistance training. Protein supplementation produced modestly larger gains in muscle mass and strength, and the extra benefit levelled off at around 1.6 g of protein per kg of body weight per day.
limitations: Pools many smaller trials with different protocols, so individual results vary.
The ~1.6 g/kg/day figure is an average; the confidence interval extended higher, so some people may benefit from more.
items.why: Your DrukFit protein target is set within this range for muscle-focused goals.

items.title: More weekly sets, more muscle? What the 2017 volume meta-analysis found
items.source_title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
items.summary: Pooling earlier studies, the authors found a graded dose-response: performing more weekly sets per muscle group tended to be associated with greater increases in muscle size.
limitations: Based on a limited number of studies, many with small samples.
Shows how results trended across studies; it doesn't set an exact best number of sets for any one person.
items.why: DrukFit adds load and reps before sets. If you plateau, adding a set to a lagging muscle is a reasonable next step.

items.title: Why DrukFit adds reps before it adds weight
items.source_title: How DrukFit's progression rules work
items.source_note: Supporting research: Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger, J Sports Sci 2017
items.summary: DrukFit suggests a heavier weight only once you hit the top of your rep range on every set at a manageable effort. Until then it asks for one more rep. Each small step is progress, and technique stays clean.
items.why: Knowing the rule makes the suggestions on your workout screen easier to trust.

items.title: Missed a workout? Do the next one, not two
items.source_title: Consistency over perfection
items.summary: Weekly targets matter more than any single day. If a session slips, DrukFit moves it to your next training day, so you never need to cram two into one.
items.why: Guilt-free consistency is what keeps a plan going for months.
